rows.verified: A food incident is a safety or quality concern about food or feed that may require action to protect consumers.
A withdrawal removes unsafe food from the supply chain before it reaches consumers.
A recall removes unsafe food after it has reached consumers and advises consumers what action to take.
Businesses should immediately withdraw or recall food believed harmful, unfit or legally non-compliant.
The food business should notify its competent authority, normally the local authority or port health authority.
The FSA incidents team should be told when unsafe food has reached consumers and a public recall may be required.
Businesses need supplier and business-customer traceability to support withdrawal and recall.

rows.verified: Food businesses are legally required to notify relevant authorities if food or feed is unsafe and must be withdrawn or recalled.
Food recalls may be issued for pathogen contamination such as listeria or salmonella.
Manufacturing faults such as plastic or metal in a product can lead to a recall.
Incorrect or missing allergen information can lead to an allergen recall.
Recall and allergy alerts state the risk and advise consumers what to do with the affected product.
Recall and allergy-alert listings are time-sensitive and must be checked against the current affected product and batch.
An allergic reaction requires immediate medical help and may also be reported to the business and local food safety team; it is case-specific evidence.
Food incidents and recalls concern specific products, businesses or supply chains and are not universal parcel-risk measurements.
